plan.title: feat(release): a new default gate ships warn-only for one release, and every refusal names a runnable remedy

narratives.Description: A new default gate can ship in a patch release and refuse work on the next hook refresh with no notice, and refusals often print a remedy that cannot be run as written, so agents read docs and runtime source to learn what a gate wants. This story adds one declaration table whose rows default to warn, one print helper that names the gate id and a runnable remedy, an advisory census of new or changed rows in release Check 5 that never stops a cut, and one test that runs each row's printed remedy from the refused state. The three dead remedies from the consumer report are the first rows, and main.md, docs/RELEASING.md and a new walkthrough page state the rule; the contract is lean 6908087379, accepted by synthesis 6908138687.
narratives.Overview:
1. One declaration table. A new consumer-visible refusal is declared in one table in `packages/core`, with an `id`, a `mode` (`warn` or `enforce`), a `remedy` (the commands to run, in order, with every argument they need) and an optional `exception` reason. A row with no `mode` is `warn`.
2. One print helper. A declared refusal prints through one helper. The line names the gate id and the remedy. In `warn` mode the work proceeds and the line says that the gate can refuse from a later release. In `enforce` mode the same line is the refusal.
3. The flip is a later one-line change. A refusal starts to refuse when its row changes to `enforce` in a later release, with its own CHANGELOG entry. A row that ships as `enforce` with no `warn` release carries an `exception` reason, and the CHANGELOG entry states that reason.
4. Advisory census. Check 5 keeps `blocking: false`. It also prints every table row that is new or changed against a baseline, which is the table at the previous release tag as selected by the pipeline. It prints the baseline it used. Each row has one of three states: warned at the baseline, absent at a baseline that was read, or unknown when the baseline cannot be read. Unknown is printed as unknown and is never reported as a missing warn release. The row's `exception` reason is printed. Its closing sentence asks for a warn-first release or a named exception. Table rows are not cut off at 20 lines. No state stops the cut.
5. Remedies run as written. One parameterized test walks the table. For each row it starts from the refusal state, runs the printed remedy exactly as printed, and retries the refused operation. A row with no such case fails the test.
6. Seed rows. The refusals that #5977 names are the first rows, in `enforce` mode: the bound pre-PR push gate, the `setup` refusal for missing hook files, and the `verify:hooks-installed` refusal that prints `deft update`. Each prints a remedy that passes item 5.
7. Rule text. `main.md` Thin Fail-Closed Design and `docs/RELEASING.md` state the rule: narrow or remove a gate before adding one; a new default refusal ships in `warn` mode for at least one release; an exception is named with its reason.
8. One walkthrough page in `content/docs/`. It gives the full command sequence for one push, one completion and one plan update, and names each gate that can refuse on the way with its remedy.
9. Accepted limit. The warn period is counted per release, not per consumer, and no per-consumer warn state is kept. A consumer who upgrades past the warn-only release meets the refusal first; that refusal names the gate id and the remedy through the helper of item 2. The rule text of item 7 states this limit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a declared refusal in `warn` mode, when its condition fires, then the work proceeds and one line names the gate id, the remedy and that the gate can refuse from a later release.
- Given a declared refusal in `enforce` mode, when its condition fires, then the refusal line names the gate id and the same remedy.
- Given a table row with no declared mode, when the table loads, then the mode of that row is `warn`.
- Given a row that is absent from a baseline that was read, with mode `enforce` and no `exception`, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists the row as having no warn release and the cut proceeds.
- Given a row that was `warn` at the baseline and is `enforce` now, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists the row as warned in the previous release.
- Given a baseline that cannot be read, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists each current row with the state unknown and the cut proceeds.
- Given a release census run, when Check 5 prints table rows, then it prints the baseline it compared against.
- Given more than 20 changed rows, when the release census runs, then every changed row is printed.
- Given any `[Unreleased]` content, when the release pipeline runs Check 5, then the disclosure returns `blocking: false`.
- Given a table row with no refusal-state case, when the test suite runs, then the remedy test fails and names the row.
- Given the bound pre-PR push gate refusal, when the printed remedy is run exactly as printed and the push is retried, then that gate does not refuse the push.
- Given the `setup` refusal for missing hook files on a fresh install, when the printed remedy is run exactly as printed and `setup` is retried, then `setup` succeeds.
- Given an installed pin that is newer than the published latest version, when the `verify:hooks-installed` refusal prints its remedy and that remedy is run exactly as printed, then the remedy does not fail as a downgrade.
- `main.md` and `docs/RELEASING.md` state the warn-first rule, the named-exception rule and the prefer-narrowing rule.
- `docs/RELEASING.md` states that a consumer who upgrades past the warn-only release meets the refusal first, with the gate id and the remedy named.
- Given a declared refusal in `enforce` mode on an install that never ran its `warn` release, when its condition fires, then the refusal line names the gate id and the remedy.
- `content/docs/` carries one walkthrough page with the command sequence for one push, one completion and one plan update.
narratives.Constraint:
- A census that stops the release (withdrawn by the operator in comment 6858622969).
- A written release rule with no hang-point in code (comment 6907284856 findings 1, 2 and 5).
- Reusing the `advise|shadow|enforce` ladder of the spec guard or the per-gate `warn|enforce` fields as a shared mechanism (comment 6907284856 finding 2).
- A remedy test that checks only that a command is registered, or one representative command (comment 6907281458 finding 3).
- Moving every existing refusal into the table in this story. That coverage is #6139.
- Consumer-local activation state, so that the warn period counts from each consumer's own first sight.
- A per-consumer policy flag to choose the mode of a declared refusal.
- A census that throws, or reports a missing warn release, when the previous release cannot be read (comment 6907376772 finding 2).
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer agent or operator meeting a Directive refusal, I want each new refusal to warn for one release first and every declared refusal to name its gate and a remedy that runs as printed, so that a patch release does not surprise me and I do not read runtime source to learn what a gate wants.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts (new): the declaration table; rows are strict JSON between begin/end markers so a past release's copy parses from git; loading defaults a missing mode to warn; lookups return results, never throw. 2. print.ts (new): one helper prints the gate id and the remedy with its arguments filled; warn mode adds that the gate can refuse from a later release and the caller proceeds; enforce mode is the refusal. 3. census.ts (new): resolve the previous release tag and read the table there through a git seam; compare with the current table; each new or changed row gets state warned, absent or unknown, plus the baseline label. 4. packages/core/src/release/consumer-readiness-disclosure.ts and run-consumer-readiness.ts: Check 5 prints every census row (no 20-line cut), the baseline, exception reasons and a closing warn-first-or-exception sentence; blocking stays false. release/pipeline.ts and release/git.ts are not touched (the running release-flow story owns them). 5. Seed rows in enforce mode: preflight-gh/pre-push.ts prints a remedy with the values the gate knows filled in (runtime/src/pre-pr-run.ts may derive git-readable defaults so the printed form runs); Taskfile.yml setup checks the hook files a fresh install deposits (_directive-run.sh, not the retired _deft-run.sh) and prints the declared remedy; verify-env/verify-hooks-installed.ts prints a remedy that is not a downgrade when the pin is newer than npm latest. 6. refusal-declarations/remedy-runs.test.ts walks every row: refused state, printed remedy run as printed (in process, with seams), retry; a row with no case fails naming the row. 7. main.md Thin Fail-Closed Design and docs/RELEASING.md state warn-first, named exception, prefer-narrowing and the skipped-release limit; content/docs/gate-walkthrough.md (new) gives the push, completion and plan-update sequences; regenerate docs/RULE-MAP.md if its sources change. 8. One test per clause plus warn_first_rule.test.ts for the doc rules; one changelog.d fragment. No new gate, stop, approval, command or consumer-facing check; no new invariant throw or numeric constant.

issueCommentThread.body:
Reshaping note from the operator before this issue is arced.

Operator direction (Scott, 2026-11-13): "we are tyring to make directive smoother in running adding mor and more gates is going the wrong way".

This issue as filed adds a gate: the release census would stop a cut when an `[Unreleased]` entry introduces a refusal without a warn-first statement. That is the wrong direction. Reshape:

- **Keep:** a new default refusal ships warn-only for one release first; the warning names the gate, the remedy and the release in which it enforces; every refusal prints a remedy that runs as written (#5977); one worked example per gate in the docs.
- **Drop:** the census stopping the release. The existing new-refusal census (Step 5, "Check 5") stays advisory: it lists the entries for operator judgment and does not block the cut.
- **Prefer:** where a gate can be narrowed or removed instead of being introduced warn-first, do that. Warn-first is the fallback for a gate that must exist.

The acceptance criterion "the release stops for operator review" is withdrawn; replace it with "the census lists the entry and the cut proceeds".

## In plain English
A new check that refuses work can ship in a patch release and start refusing on the next hook refresh. The consumer learns about it when a push or a write is refused. The refusal often does not say what to run, or it names a command that cannot be run as printed, so agents read docs and compiled runtime code to find out what the gate wants. The issue asks for a release rule: a new default refusal warns for one release before it can refuse, the warning names the gate, the remedy and the release in which it will refuse, every refusal prints a remedy that runs as written, and the docs carry one worked example per gate. The operator then reshaped the issue (comment 6858622969): the release census must stay advisory and must not stop a cut, and narrowing or removing a gate is preferred to introducing one warn-first. The open question is whether a rule with no blocking check actually holds, and what the smallest mechanical support is that does not itself become a gate.

## Pains
- P1 — A new default refusal can arrive in a patch release and refuse work on the next hook refresh, with no notice and no warn-only period.
- P2 — A refusal does not name the gate, the remedy and what the gate wants in one place, so agents read docs and compiled runtime source to find out (a consumer report in the issue body counts 268 such reads in one week).
- P3 — Printed remedy commands cannot be run as written (#5977: `deft update` becomes a refused downgrade; `deft pre-pr:run` with no arguments exits 2; `task setup` needs a retired hook helper).
- P4 — There is no worked example per gate: the full command sequence for one push, one completion and one plan update.
- P5 — The fix must not add a gate. The new-refusal census stays advisory, lists the entry, and the cut proceeds (operator reshaping note, comment 6858622969).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA (claims, to be re-verified)
- `packages/core/src/release/consumer-readiness-disclosure.ts` (1-74): Check 5 is a regex over the `[Unreleased]` text (`fail-closed`, `refuses to`, `MUST NOT`, `new refusal` and similar). It returns `blocking: false` and prints "Each new refusal needs remediation text and an escape hatch. This is not a computed verdict."
- `packages/core/src/release/pipeline.ts` (540-560): the pipeline prints that disclosure at Step 5; "checks 5-6 disclosure never block".
- `packages/core/src/policy/spec-guard.ts` (31-53): the `advise|shadow|enforce` ladder is specific to `plan.policy.specGuard`, with default `advise` and a shadow attestation before `enforce`. It is not a shared ladder.
- `packages/core/src/test-boundary/policy.ts` (38, 145-183) and `packages/core/src/class-checks/evaluate.ts` (299): two more gates carry their own `enforcementMode: "warn" | "enforce"`; test-boundary defaults to `warn`. `packages/runtime/src/verify-forward-coverage.ts` (22-25) is warn-first on diff coverage. Each gate owns its mode; there is no shared gate registry and no shared mode type.
- `packages/core/src/preflight-gh/pre-push.ts` (312, 361, 494): the bound pre-PR push gate still prints "Recovery: deft pre-pr:run then retry push", the line #5977 reports as not runnable with no arguments.
- `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/recovery_target_resolves.test.ts`: an existing content test proves that recovery targets named in three carrier files resolve. It covers file targets in docs, not the remedy commands that gates print at run time.
- A grep of `packages/core/src` and `packages/runtime/src` outside tests finds about 140 lines that print `Recovery: ` and 59 that name `deft update`. There is no shared helper that all of them go through.
- `main.md` (88-98) Thin Fail-Closed Design (#3265): "one fail-closed deterministic check with one remediation string" for a first ship. This is the standing rule that the warn-first rule would amend.

## Related issues (described content)
- #5977 (open): printed recovery commands cannot be run.
- #6139 (open): every write-gate deny prints exactly one next command, resolved from a reason code, with advisory strengths printing the same line.
- #5914 (open, accepted design on its own thread): one refusal whose remedy names a task that does not exist.

## Operator direction recorded for this arc
The operator wants Directive to run more smoothly. A fix that removes steps, PRs and stops is preferred to one that adds a gate. A new refusal needs a reason that no existing control covers.

## Bound remedy
1. One declaration table. A new consumer-visible refusal is declared in one table in `packages/core`, with an `id`, a `mode` (`warn` or `enforce`), a `remedy` (the commands to run, in order, with every argument they need) and an optional `exception` reason. A row with no `mode` is `warn`.
2. One print helper. A declared refusal prints through one helper. The line names the gate id and the remedy. In `warn` mode the work proceeds and the line says that the gate can refuse from a later release. In `enforce` mode the same line is the refusal.
3. The flip is a later one-line change. A refusal starts to refuse when its row changes to `enforce` in a later release, with its own CHANGELOG entry. A row that ships as `enforce` with no `warn` release carries an `exception` reason, and the CHANGELOG entry states that reason.
4. Advisory census. Check 5 keeps `blocking: false`. It also prints every table row that is new or changed against a baseline, which is the table at the previous release tag as selected by the pipeline. It prints the baseline it used. Each row has one of three states: warned at the baseline, absent at a baseline that was read, or unknown when the baseline cannot be read. Unknown is printed as unknown and is never reported as a missing warn release. The row's `exception` reason is printed. Its closing sentence asks for a warn-first release or a named exception. Table rows are not cut off at 20 lines. No state stops the cut.
5. Remedies run as written. One parameterized test walks the table. For each row it starts from the refusal state, runs the printed remedy exactly as printed, and retries the refused operation. A row with no such case fails the test.
6. Seed rows. The refusals that #5977 names are the first rows, in `enforce` mode: the bound pre-PR push gate, the `setup` refusal for missing hook files, and the `verify:hooks-installed` refusal that prints `deft update`. Each prints a remedy that passes item 5.
7. Rule text. `main.md` Thin Fail-Closed Design and `docs/RELEASING.md` state the rule: narrow or remove a gate before adding one; a new default refusal ships in `warn` mode for at least one release; an exception is named with its reason.
8. One walkthrough page in `content/docs/`. It gives the full command sequence for one push, one completion and one plan update, and names each gate that can refuse on the way with its remedy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Given a declared refusal in `warn` mode, when its condition fires, then the work proceeds and one line names the gate id, the remedy and that the gate can refuse from a later release.
- Given a declared refusal in `enforce` mode, when its condition fires, then the refusal line names the gate id and the same remedy.
- Given a table row with no declared mode, when the table loads, then the mode of that row is `warn`.
- Given a row that is absent from a baseline that was read, with mode `enforce` and no `exception`, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists the row as having no warn release and the cut proceeds.
- Given a row that was `warn` at the baseline and is `enforce` now, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists the row as warned in the previous release.
- Given a baseline that cannot be read, when the release census runs, then Check 5 lists each current row with the state unknown and the cut proceeds.
- Given a release census run, when Check 5 prints table rows, then it prints the baseline it compared against.
- Given more than 20 changed rows, when the release census runs, then every changed row is printed.
- Given any `[Unreleased]` content, when the release pipeline runs Check 5, then the disclosure returns `blocking: false`.
- Given a table row with no refusal-state case, when the test suite runs, then the remedy test fails and names the row.
- Given the bound pre-PR push gate refusal, when the printed remedy is run exactly as printed and the push is retried, then that gate does not refuse the push.
- Given the `setup` refusal for missing hook files on a fresh install, when the printed remedy is run exactly as printed and `setup` is retried, then `setup` succeeds.
- Given an installed pin that is newer than the published latest version, when the `verify:hooks-installed` refusal prints its remedy and that remedy is run exactly as printed, then the remedy does not fail as a downgrade.
- `main.md` and `docs/RELEASING.md` state the warn-first rule, the named-exception rule and the prefer-narrowing rule.

## Summary

A new default gate can arrive in a patch release and start refusing work on the next hook refresh, with no notice. Consumers find out when a push or a write is refused, and then read the runtime source to learn what the gate wants.

Directive already has the pattern for doing this safely: the spec-drift guard ladder `advise|shadow|enforce` (#1589), and warn-first forward coverage (#3514).

## Consumer impact

On a consumer project, a new default gate arrived in a patch release and applied on the next hook refresh. In one week, agents read Directive docs or source 268 times to find out what a gate wanted, 206 of them in compiled runtime code.

## Expected

A release rule, checked mechanically:

- A gate that adds a new consumer-visible refusal ships warn-only (advise or shadow) for at least one release before it can refuse by default. The warning names the gate, the remedy and the release in which it will enforce.
- Exceptions (a security fix that must refuse now) are named in the CHANGELOG entry with the reason.
- The release pipeline's new-refusal census (Step 5, "Check 5") already lists `[Unreleased]` lines that may introduce a refusal. Make it require, for each one, either a warn-first statement or a named exception.
- Every refusal prints a remedy that can be run as written (#5977), and each gate has one worked example in the docs: the full command sequence for one push, one completion and one plan update.

## Acceptance

- Given an `[Unreleased]` entry that introduces a default refusal with no warn-first statement and no exception, when the release census runs, then it reports the entry and the release stops for operator review.
- Given a gate in its warn-only release, when its condition fires, then the work proceeds and the warning names the enforce release.
- Docs carry one worked example per gate named above.

Refs #1589. Refs #3265. Refs #5977.
